source.title: OptiRoulette Optimizer: A New Stochastic Meta-Optimizer for up to 5.3x Faster Convergence

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It notes that figure slots are placeholders, but Tables 1–7 report results.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out performance for a new optimizer-selection policy against a fixed AdamW baseline. This bears on optimizer effects on generalization, but does not isolate the comparisons specified in V4.
record.gate_note: The study compares OptiRoulette with AdamW and reports test metrics. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout, sharpness measures, or removing memorized examples. Its cited optimizer results are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study discusses stage-dependent optimizer generalization but tests none of V1–V8. Its comparison is OptiRoulette versus fixed AdamW, without a standalone SGD comparator or an Adam-to-SGD transition. Better held-out accuracy for this new policy does not establish V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors emphasize more reliable attainment of high validation-accuracy targets and improved test accuracy against fixed AdamW across five suites. They acknowledge that broader optimizer baselines and additional benchmarks remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 17-epoch SGD warmup followed by epoch-level stochastic selection among a restricted optimizer pool, with transition learning-rate scaling and pool replacement; compares this policy with a single AdamW baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and benchmark setting; the paper reports different accuracy gains across the five datasets. Its recipe was selected through internal cross-dataset tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five image-classification suites and 10 paired seeds, OptiRoulette improves test accuracy over fixed AdamW. Table 7 reports positive paired accuracy differences with p < 0.001 on every suite.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The internally tuned SGD-warmup and stochastic optimizer-selection recipe improves held-out accuracy over the reported fixed AdamW baseline in these settings.

record.problems: Only a single AdamW baseline is used; the paper says stronger multi-baseline comparisons remain to be completed. The reported optimizer preset was selected from internal cross-dataset tuning. The study covers five image-classification suites and does not evaluate LLM workloads. Several figures are placeholders, though the reported test accuracy values are tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: No required table results omitted. Table 4 precision, recall, and F1 are excluded because the paper says roulette and simple mode use different averaging methods, and accuracy is the primary like-for-like metric.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.

Adaptive versus SGD-family generalization under limited or broader tuning; decoupled weight-decay effects; Adam-to-SGD switching; word-level language modeling. OptiRoulette instead starts with SGD and then excludes it from the sampled pool.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout comparisons, underfitting, small-data effects, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reported accuracy values and confidence intervals are transcribed correctly. These method-performance comparisons should not serve as evidence for V1–V8. The preset was selected through internal cross-dataset tuning; the paper does not isolate optimizer switching from warmup, learning rates, or stabilization rules. No additional results bearing on a listed version appear in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum under limited tuning; broader tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
